text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition better, can you describe the appearance of the rash and tell me exactly when it started appearing in relation to your fever and other symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text: The progression from a facial rash sparing the perioral area to a body rash is very characteristic. Have you noticed any joint pain or swelling in her hands or feet?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Mildly pruritic rash on trunk and extremities. I also have Low-grade fever, Rhinorrhea, Headache, Facial rash not involving the perioral skin.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical presentation of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a pruritic body rash is highly suggestive of Erythema Infectiosum, also known as Fifth Disease. To confirm this, I will request a visual examination of the characteristic "slapped cheek" appearance and the reticular body rash.

The clinical picture of a facial rash sparing the perioral area followed by a pruritic reticular body rash is classic for Parvovirus B19 infection. Given the strong clinical evidence, I am ready to diagnose.
